primary_work.title: Causal Representation Learning from General Environments under Nonparametric Mixing
primary_work.code_status: public runnable code located; no release or immutable dependency lockfile established

decision: NARROWED BEYOND GENERAL-ENVIRONMENT NONPARAMETRIC CRL — NOT ADOPTED
rejected_claims: unknown intervention type or target labels alone make language necessary for causal representation identification
general environment variation as an identification signal is a new language-grounding contribution
language that names or predicts an environment signature jointly identifies raw utterance equivalence and intervention targets
task success, next-state prediction, environment classification, or language-shuffle gaps prove residual target-partition identification
remaining_rq: After applying general-environment CRL under the strongest valid sufficient-change assumptions, can a preregistered externally fixed language law distinguish models with identical environment-conditioned observation and transition distributions but different residual intervention-target partitions, while jointly identifying raw-utterance equivalence and eliminating all joint language/target recodings?
